context.title: Context: SUSTAIN-NOBILITY (redesign proposal)
context.h1: The rules and standards around the question

intro.label: AgentiCCells's summary
intro.text: Why the question matters, from official sources. Every date and status on this page is read from data/research.json at build time and shown with its source, publisher and read date. Where a source has not been read, nothing is shown in its place.

eu.label: AgentiCCells's summary
eu.text: The EU AI Act applies in stages, and an amending regulation, the Digital Omnibus on AI, has moved some of them. It gives SMEs simpler documentation and priority access to regulatory sandboxes, and caps their fines at the lower of two amounts.

uk.label: AgentiCCells's summary
uk.text: The UK has no single AI law. Existing regulators apply five cross-sector principles; the government asked regulators to publish plans for supporting safe AI innovation, and chose to write governance guidance for SMEs instead of publishing its AI Management Essentials tool. The ICO's guidance says most uses of AI will need a data protection impact assessment.

standards.label: AgentiCCells's summary
standards.text: Two voluntary frameworks are widely used to organise AI governance evidence: ISO/IEC 42001, a certifiable AI management system standard, and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, built around Govern, Map, Measure and Manage.

evidence.label: AgentiCCells's summary
evidence.text: Taken together, the sources suggest what an SME may be asked to show: a record of the AI systems it uses and their risk class, AI literacy measures, impact assessments where personal data is involved, transparency notices and, for high-risk uses, human oversight.

their_alignment.label: AgentiCCells's summary
their_alignment.text: Their Our Tool page says the check is aligned with the main UK and EU regulators relevant to AI, without naming them.

about_proposal.title: About this proposal
text: This site is a redesign proposal for SUSTAIN-NOBILITY Advisory Ltd, made by AgentiCCells with their agreement. It presents the same company, offer and method as their current site, written again for clarity. It is not their official site.
Their words are quoted as published, with the link and the date we read them. Lines marked as AgentiCCells's summary are ours. Nothing here is a new claim about clients, results or prices.
Five alternative designs show the same words in different layouts.

proposals.intro: Suggestions from AgentiCCells for SUSTAIN-NOBILITY to consider. These are our proposals, not their claims.

items.text: Proposal: Lead with the question the site already owns, "Can you prove it is governed responsibly?", and make evidence you can show the thread through every page.
Proposal: Use one product name everywhere. Their site uses both Readiness Check and Health Check.
Proposal: Give SMEs and advisers two clear paths from the home page, with Partner Licensing as the adviser offer.
Proposal: Name the frameworks the check maps to, once the company confirms the mapping, in place of 'the main UK and EU regulators'.
Proposal: Add a short, dated panel on what changed this year in EU and UK rules, with the date it was last checked.
Proposal: Say plainly what each plan delivers and whether prices will be published.
Proposal: Carry the Disclaimer's plain words into the main copy: the check is indicative, not legal advice or certification.
Proposal: Correct small wording slips on the current site, such as 'assess responsibly governance maturity' and 'concommitantly', and complete the sentence about the real-time diagnostic.
Proposal: Publish an accessibility statement and move the Terms of Use to their own address.
